Ansar Ali, Advocate ------ For the petitioner 
Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Advocate with S.M. Amin Azhar, Advocate ------ For the opposite parties
parties:
Wasef Ali Chowdhury & Others
Vs.
Sekandar Rahman & Others
full_judgment:
Syed Muhammad Husain, J: Following the terms or a Waqf nama to give effect to the intents of the Waqif, an order was passed by the Administrator of Waqf on 22-7-71 in E.G. No. 1308 when a minor boy was substituted as a Mutwalli in place of a deceased Mutwalli alleged to be the maternal grandfather of such substituted minor Mutwalli, during whose minority his mother being the daughter of the deceased Mutwalli was appointed as the guardian Mutwalli till the minor attains majority. Upon receipt of the notice of substitution of a minor Mutwalli and appointment of a guardian Mutwalli by the Administrator of Waqf, four persons interested in the Waqf, alleging to be beneficiaries thereof filed an objection before the Administrator of Waqf who upon hearing the parties concerned rejected the prayer for cancellation of the order for appointment of a Mutwalli guardian. The said objectors preferred Civil Misc. Nos. 81 and 82 of 1972 against the order of the Administrator of Waqf before the District Judge of Rajshahi who by Judgment dated 30th May 1979 set aside the order of the Administrator of Waqf dated 22-2-71 and cancelled the substitution of a minor Mutwalli and appointment of a guardian wall. Against the aforesaid decision of the District Judge of Rajshahi, Misc. Case Nos. 2 and 3 of 1979 were preferred before the same District Judge of Rajshahi on behalf of the Guardian Mutwalli for the Review of the previous judgment of District Judge who upon Review of the judgment passed previously in Civil Misc. Appeal No. 81 and 82 of 1972 on 30th May, 1979 set aside the aforesaid Judgment and restored the order of the Administrator o Waqf and confirmed the substitution of a minor Mutwalli and appointment of a guardian Mutwalli till such period that the minor attains majority. Against the aforesaid judgment of the District Judge of Rajshahi by order No.80 dated 30th August, 1979 in the aforesaid Civil Misc. Case Nos. 2 and 3 of 1979, the aforesaid four beneficiaries of the Waqf preferred two Civil Revision Cases before the High Court Division and obtained these two Rules which are being heard and disposed of analogously. 

 3. So far as Review of any Judgment passed in an Appeal under the concluding provision of Section 43 of Waqf Ordinance No. 1 of 1962 is concerned, admittedly it being a civil proceeding as contemplated under Section 141 of C.P.C., the provision for Review as contemplated under-Order 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure will be applicable in the present case. Sub-Rule 1 of Rule 1 of order 47 of the C.P.C. says that any person considering himself aggrieved by any order from which no appeal has been preferred or from which no appeal is allowed, may apply for Review of the Judgment of the Court which made the order only on the following limited grounds: 

 4. Admittedly in the present case there was no occasion of any discovery of any new matter or evidence which was not or could not be produced at the time when the earlier Judgment was pronounced by the District Judge. As to the question whether there was any mistake or error apparent on the face of the record which invariably means a mistake or error o f fact, it must be said that there was none in the present case. Now the only question is as to whether there was any other sufficient reason for the Review of the Judgment of the District Judge. The Review was allowed by the learned District Judge only on the ground that the previous Judgment by the District Judge was made upon a misconception of the provision of Section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance No.1 of 1962. Considering such position it must be held that there was a divergence of opinion about the interpretation of a provision of law by the same District Judge on the same question in the same case on two occasions. It has been submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the same District Judge sat on an appeal as against its own previous judgment in the same case. In the present case the same District Judge hearing the case twice between the same parties on same matter changed his earlier opinion about the provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance No. 1 of 1962. In view of such facts and circumstances of the case the question now is whether the learned District Judge could Review his own judgment on such ground which can be called a sufficient reason as contemplated under Sub-Rule 1 of the Rule 1 of Order 47 of the C.P.C. 

 5. In order to decide this question it is to be decided whether the original order of the Administrator of Waqf passed on 22-7-71 was correct in view of the provision of Section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance No. 1 of 1962 Section 43 says that in the case of any Waqf of which there is no Mutwalli or the successor to the office of a Mutwalli is a minor, the Administrator may for such period as he deemed fit appoint a person to act as Mutwalli. In order to ascertain the intention of the legislature with regard to Section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance No.1 of 1962, reference must be made to Sub-Section 6 of Section 2 of the said Waqf Ordinance No.1 of 1962 wherein a Mutwalli has been defined as any person appointed by a competent authority as a Mutwalli of any Waqf including the Guardian of a Mutwalli who is a minor. Considering the aforesaid provisions of Section 43 read with Sub-Section 6 of Section 2 of Waqf Ordinance No.1 of 1962 it must be said that during the minority of a Mutwalli, the guardian of the minor could be appointed to act as a Mutwalli by the Administrator of Waqf till such period when the minor attains majority. In the present case there .is no dispute that after the death of the previous Mutwalli, his minor grandson through his daughter would be the Mutwalli, if and when he otherwise attains majority. It is also not disputed. That during the minority o f any child the mother is the most immediate natural guardian of the minor, particularly when the guardianship is never challenged by any interested person. In such circumstances it can be safely and unmistakably said that the Administrator of Waqf rightly substituted a minor Mutwalli and till such minor attains majority the Administrator of Waqf rightly appointed the minor's mother as the guardian Mutwalli. 

 6. It has however been submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that while substituting a minor Mutwalli and appointing a guardian Mutwalli, the Administrator of Waqf did not issue any previous notice to the beneficiaries. Section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance No.1 of 1962 says that the Administrator may appoint a person to act as a Mutwalli with notice to persons interested in the Waqf. This does not mean that the notices must be issued prior to the appointment of any person to act as a Mutwalli. The only obligation on the part of the Administrator is to notify all persons interested in the Waqf about the appointment of any person to act as Mutwalli. After receipt of notice, any person interested in the Waqf, may object to any appointment of any Mutwalli by the Administrator of Waqf. In the present case such notice was evidently given to the persons interested in the Waqf otherwise the present petitioners being the beneficiaries of the Waqf could not have filed objection before the Administrator of the Waqf challenging the Substitution of a minor Mutwalli and appointment of a guardian Mutwalli which was heard and disposed of on merit in presence of the parties concerned by the Administrator of Waqf. In such circumstances the Administrator of Waqf made the necessary order for substitution of a minor Mutwalli and appointment of a guardian Mutwalli with notice to persons interested in the Waqf as contemplated under Section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance No.1 of 1962. 

 7. Thus it must be held that the order made by the Administrator of Waqf on 22-7-71 in D.C. No. 1308 is in full conformity with the provision of section 43 of Waqf Ordinance 1 of 1962. In such circumstances it must also be held that on the interpretation of Section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance No.1 of 1962, the previous decision of the District Judge of Rajshahi was invariably wrong and the subsequent decision was correct. In that view it can be safely said to be a sufficient reason for the District Judge to Review its own previous Judgment on that account. Be that as it may the Revisional Jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Section 115 of the C.P.C. is discretionary which must be exercised not only in accordance with law but also on grounds of equity and ends of justice. In the present case the Administrator of Waqf did not commit any illegality in passing an order for substitution of a minor Mutwalli and appointment of a guardian Mutwalli as contemplated under section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance No.1 of 1962. As there was no miscarriage of justice on that account, rather it caused full justice according to law, this court exercising its discretionary revisional Jurisdiction will refuse to interfere with the Judgment passed by the District Judge of Rajshahi Reviewing and correcting its own decision in the light of the legal implication of Section 43 of Waqf Ordinance 1 of 1962.
